extracted.intended_audience: KIPO patent examiners, patent applicants, and patent attorneys (Korean patent prosecution context)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for classifying patent applications (IPC/CPC), publication (laying-open), requesting and starting examination, examination order/deferment, and applicable deadlines under the Korean Patent Office procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: IPC identification formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Use boldface type for invention information, regular (non-bold) type for additional information, italic style for extension level, and indexing code used only for additional information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates how to present IPC symbols and which typographic styles indicate invention vs additional information; version/directive year-month appear in square brackets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional information optionality (indexing code or classification symbols)
rubrics_metrics.description: Additional information is an option to complement invention information and can be given by either indexing code or classification symbols.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indexing codes are designated based on an indexing classification table categorized by technical functions (purpose, use, structure, material, manufacturing process, disposal process, control measure, etc.) not included in the classification place. After designating a classification symbol, an indexing code may be designated additionally for technical subject-matter useful to search.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality due to national security must be stated
rubrics_metrics.description: If the invention described in the specification is required to be confidential due to national security, such requirement shall be stated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Part Ⅶ, chapter 3 for more details (i.e., applications requiring confidentiality are excluded from public lay-open).

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification inheritance for divisional/converted/domestic/treaty priority applications
rubrics_metrics.description: The classification of an original (parent) application shall be identified first and, except when classifications of the original obviously fail to correspond to the later-filed application, it is preferable to remain the same classification of the original application as main classification while designating the newly granted classification as sub-classification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to divisional applications, converted applications, domestic priority claim applications, treaty priority claim applications, and applications of lawful right holders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification rule for apparatus vs method
rubrics_metrics.description: In principle, use the classification place for either an apparatus or a method if a pertinent place exists; if an apparatus has no classification place, use the method in the apparatus, and vice versa; if neither exists, use the place for the product manufactured with the apparatus or method.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies fallbacks for missing places: apparatus → method → product.

rubrics_metrics.name: Products classification by product, function, or use
rubrics_metrics.description: Manufactured product shall be classified with the place pertinent to the product. If no such place exists, use an appropriate function-oriented place; if no function-oriented place, classify based on the use of the manufactured product.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hierarchy: product-centric classification preferred; function-oriented or use-based classification are successive fallbacks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multistage process or plant classification
rubrics_metrics.description: A multistage process or plant shall be classified with the place pertinent to the composition; if no such classification place exists, use the place for the output produced from the composition. Where constituents have individual characteristics, each constituent shall also be classified with its classification place.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the composition has no intrinsic characteristics but its constituent has, the composition shall not be classified (i.e., classify constituents instead). Example given: class B09B.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specifics/structural parts classification
rubrics_metrics.description: If structural or functional specifics/parts in the claimed invention are used only for a certain apparatus, classify into the place for that apparatus. If such specifics/parts can be used for more than two apparatuses, classify into the place for those specifics/parts. If no place exists for them, classify in place for the relevant apparatus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decision depends on breadth of applicability: single-apparatus use → apparatus place; multi-apparatus (>2) use → parts place.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification when a technical subject-matter relates to multiple groups
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a single technical subject-matter is related to more than two groups directly and intrinsically, classify into the place for all the related groups. If included in more than two groups of equal level under the same main group, classify into the place for a higher hierarchic group; except if inclusion into multiple groups is of little importance for search and is simply relevant to combination of elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guides when to assign multiple classifications versus a higher-level grouping; balances search usefulness against redundancy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification of chemical compounds (Section C)
rubrics_metrics.description: Technical subject-matter of chemical compounds (organic, inorganic or polymer) shall be classified into the relevant place for Section C pursuant to intrinsic characteristics (i.e., chemical structure). If the compound is related to a field of use and the field of use is essential content, classify the field of use into the place if a pertinent place exists. If the subject-matter is related only to the use of the compound, only the field of use can be classified into the place.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritizes intrinsic chemical characteristics; field-of-use classification only when essential or when compound’s role is use-related.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification of mixtures or compositions
rubrics_metrics.description: Mixtures or compositions shall be classified into the relevant place pursuant to their intrinsic features (examples: C03C for glass composition, C04B for cement/ceramic composition, C22C for alloy composition). If no relevant place exists, classify pursuant to their use or application. If essential characteristics reside in the use/application, classify both the mixture/composition per se and their application/use into the place of the field of use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains when to classify by intrinsic composition vs by application/use; gives explicit class examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification of manufacture or treatment of compounds
rubrics_metrics.description: When the claimed invention relates to manufacture or treatment of compounds, the compounds per se shall be classified; methods of manufacture/treatment shall also be classified if pertinent places exist. General methods to manufacture or treat compounds shall be classified in the place if the relevant place exists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguishes between compound per se and processes; include both where relevant and where classification places exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification of Markush-type chemical compounds
rubrics_metrics.description: For Markush-type chemical compounds generally defined in a formula, the general chemical formula shall be classified individually if the formula has a few relevant places (for example, less than 5). Specified compounds (designated by structure or identified by properties or described in an example) that are per se in the claimed invention, outputs of a claimed process, or their derivatives, shall be classified in each relevant place.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines 'specified' as (i) designated by structure/title/formula or inferred from a specific reactant, or (ii) identified with physical properties or described in a detailed example. Use multiple classifications when specific compounds are singled out.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification of combinatorial libraries
rubrics_metrics.description: In combinatorial libraries with many compounds, biological entities, or substances, IPC shall be granted to each individual compound pursuant to the same method as classification of Markush-type compounds. Characteristics of the entire library shall be classified into combinatorial chemistry (C40B).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Individual-compound classification plus a library-level classification (C40B) for the whole library characteristics.

rubrics_metrics.name: CPC adoption and advantages
rubrics_metrics.description: Cooperative Patent Classification (CPC) was developed jointly by USPTO and EPO to improve efficiency of prior art searching; KIPO has used CPC since January 2015. CPC makes access to prior art expanded and easier and allows search of documents in various languages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains historical origin and practical benefits of CPC for searching and multilingual access.

rubrics_metrics.name: CPC structure: main trunk, indexing codes (2000 series), and Section Y
rubrics_metrics.description: The CPC table is divided into three sections: Main trunk, Indexing codes (2000 series), and Section Y. Compared to IPC, CPC has 2000 series and Section Y providing additional information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indexing codes provide orthogonal/breakdown indexing; Section Y handles technical subject matter not present in IPC.

rubrics_metrics.name: CPC main trunk hierarchy and notation
rubrics_metrics.description: The CPC main trunk has hierarchical structure like IPC (section, class, subclass, main group, subgroup). CPC subgroup notation adds digits/dashes allowing finer classification; information added only in the CPC because there is no corresponding IPC place is indicated in brackets { }.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subgroup is minimum unit for search; finer breakdown is possible because of extra digits/words compared to IPC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indexing codes (2000 series) are non-obligatory unless directed
rubrics_metrics.description: Indexing classification table of the CPC (2000 series) originates from IPC indexing and EPO ICO/KW. Indexing codes (starting with 2000) are attached only to additional information and classifying with indexing codes is not obligatory unless there is extra direction in the main trunk and its definition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ICO-based groups include breakdown indexing codes (more finely broken down from main trunk) and orthogonal indexing codes (different principle from breakdown). No 2000-series symbols in Section Y.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section Y purpose and allocation
rubrics_metrics.description: Section Y was introduced by the EPO to deal with technical subject matter necessary but not present in IPC; symbols of Section Y are allocated as additional information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides examples of Section Y titles (e.g., Y02 for climate change related tech, Y04 for ICT impacting another technical field, Y10 for USPC mutual reference tech collection). Section Y contains ~7,000 classification symbols.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hierarchy indicated by dots/indentation in CPC subgroup titles
rubrics_metrics.description: Hierarchy among subgroups is determined by the number of dots coming ahead of each title; hierarchy is indicated only by indentation level, not by subgroup digits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: A01B 1/02 (one dot) is higher level than 1/04 (two dots), even though each subgroup has two digits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation rules for group titles (English vs Korean)
rubrics_metrics.description: Two translation types: for English, if subgroup title starts with a capitalized alphabet, it is deemed complete; if not, deemed subordinated to higher hierarchy. For Korean, since no case distinction, understand according to context or English version.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scope of CPC groups is exclusive despite translation differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of laying open of application (publication)
rubrics_metrics.description: Laying open of application publishes the application after a prescribed period from filing to prevent overlaps in investment and research and to make the invention part of common knowledge for industrial development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Laying open separates publication from the examination timeline to avoid devaluation and to promote social contribution of technical information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Laying-open date rules (1.5 years, priority, divisional treatment, early publication)
rubrics_metrics.description: An application shall be laid open after expiration of 1 year and 6 months from the filing date. For applications claiming priority, the period starts from the filing date of the first country application or the filing date of the prior-filed application (earliest if more than 2 priority claims). A divisional or converted application is deemed filed on the same date as the parent, so the laying-open period starts from parent filing date; if divisional filed after 1.5 years from parent, it shall be laid open without delay. An applicant may request early publication (Form (xxv)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies how priority and divisional filing dates affect the 1.5-year publication clock; early publication procedure available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusions from laying open (confidentiality/public order/claims etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications shall generally be laid open, but excluded are applications that do not include claims as prescribed (Article 42(5)), applications whose registration is published, or applications invalidated, withdrawn, abandoned, or decided to reject. Also not laid open if they contain matters requiring confidentiality due to national security or are liable to contravene public order or morality or harm public health (Patent Act Article 64, Enforcement Decree Article 19(3)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives statutory bases and an example concerning prior-filed applications used for domestic priority claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and media for laying open
rubrics_metrics.description: The application is laid open in the online patent gazette on KIPO website; the same publication can be found in DVD-ROM and via KIPI website.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies distribution channels for published applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effects of laying open: warning/compensation and prior art status
rubrics_metrics.description: After laying open, applicant may give a warning with documents stating the claimed invention to a person practicing the invention as a business and may claim compensation equivalent to normal licensing fees from the date of warning or the date the person knew the application had been laid open until patent registration; however, right to claim compensation may not be exercised until patent right registration. Laid-open application achieves status as prior art pursuant to Article 29(1) subparagraphs and can be used for other applications pursuant to Article 29(3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Warning/compensation rights available but exercisable only after registration; laid-open becomes prior art for novelty/obviousness considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for examination — general admissibility and requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for examination shall be made only for an application pending in KIPO; it is allowed only once per application and, once admitted, cannot be withdrawn. A valid request survives legal incapacity (e.g., death). An applicant may request examination only if a specification including claims is attached, or in foreign-language cases, only if a Korean translation pursuant to Article 42-3(2) is provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures applications are complete (claims/translation) before requesting examination; one-time, irrevocable request rule emphasized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third-party requests for examination allowed
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person, including third parties without interests in the application, may request examination of a patent application; incompetent persons (minors) must proceed via legal representatives. An association or foundation not a juridical person but with designated representative may file a request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broad standing for third-party examination requests; procedural notes for legal representatives and organizational filers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing limits for requesting examination and consequences of delay
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for examination shall be filed within three years (five years for applications filed on or before ’17.2.28) from the filing date. For divisional/converted applications, a person may request examination within thirty days from their filing date even after expiration of the three-year period. For international applications, the request shall be made within three years from the international filing date. Failure to request within prescribed period causes the application to be deemed withdrawn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets hard statutory timelines and special rules for old filings and divisionals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure and fees for requesting examination
rubrics_metrics.description: File a written request (Form (xxii) in the Enforcement Rules) to the Commissioner of KIPO and pay the examination fee. If the number of claims increases because of amendments after a third-party request, the applicant shall pay the fee corresponding to the increased number of claims; if fees for increased claims are not paid, the applicant is instructed to pay and failure to make additional payment may invalidate the amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative steps and financial consequences for claim-count changes after filing a request initiated by a third party.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effects of a request for examination on proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: An application whose examination is requested shall be examined by an examiner; pendency can be terminated only by patent registration or rejection unless invalidated/withdrawn/abandoned. If the request is made before laying-open, the purpose of the request shall be published in the patent gazette upon publication (or immediately if request made after laying-open). Applicants lacking claims must amend to include claims by prescribed date in response to notification. If a third party filed the request, the Commissioner shall notify the applicant; the examiner shall notify the third party of the final decision (including withdrawal/abandonment).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notification duties between KIPO, applicant, and third-party requester; amendment obligations to include claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination start — verifying classification and examiner allocation
rubrics_metrics.description: An examiner shall verify whether the application is classified appropriately pursuant to CPC/IPC and whether the application is within the scope of his/her patent classification in charge. If the examiner is in charge of main classification he should proceed; he may allocate to another examiner in charge of sub-classification after consultation; if allocated incorrectly, reallocate or apply for correction of classification; if reallocation is not made properly, ask Patent Examination Policy Division to correct classification and reallocate the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures correct technical expertise alignment; gives steps for reallocation and correction of classification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner disqualification and transfer rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner shall review whether he/she falls under disqualification reasons stated in Article 148( subparagraphs ) or shall be excluded because a person with less than 2 years experience as an examiner had worked at the organization filing the application for the last three years before appointment. If disqualified, transfer the application to another examiner in charge of the most similar technical classification with approval of the director of Examination Bureau.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protects impartiality and avoids conflicts of interest; uses statutory disqualification grounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination order and priority rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Examination starts in the order of request for examination per an examiner or classification (subclass). If date of examination request is identical for an examiner or classification, a patent application shall have priority over a utility model registration. If applications are of the same kind, the application with earlier filing date has priority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines queuing and tie-breaking rules; 'start of examination' includes first notices such as grounds for rejection, amendment request, consultation, or certified copy of decision to grant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Divisional/converted application examination order specifics
rubrics_metrics.description: Divisional or converted applications shall be examined in order of their examination request. However, if filed after examination request of the parent, their examination starts in order of the parent’s examination request. If parent is divided/converted after examination started, the divisional/converted examination shall start before the later of either 3 months from the divisional/converted examination request or 2 months from receipt of application documents; divisional/converted of an expedited parent follow the parent's order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Governs interplay between parent and divisional timings and special handling for expedited cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Circumstances allowing examiners to defer examination
rubrics_metrics.description: An examiner may defer examination where: (①) a prior-filed or conflicting application is not laid open or not requested for examination; ② a prior-filed domestic priority claim is prior to withdrawal period pursuant to Article 56; ③ a trial or litigation related to the application is pending; ④ a search is outsourced or advice of outside specialists/consultation is required; ⑤ the period for submitting evidential documents for priority claims under the treaty has not elapsed; ⑥ other needs for deferment (see Part 5 Chapter 3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists statutory and practical reasons allowing deferment of start of substantive examination to prevent premature action or coordination with related proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing deadlines for reexamination, expedited examination, and other timelines
rubrics_metrics.description: For applications on request for reexamination after rejection or remanded from appeal, examiner shall begin examination within one month from receipt of application documents (report unavoidable delays). For expedited-examination requests, the examiner shall determine whether it falls under expedited category within 7 days from receipt; examination shall begin within 2 months from delivery of the notice of the examiner’s decision (or within 4 months for certain expedited grounds). Various other deadlines for prior-art search, delivery of decisions, amendment periods, and resumed examination are prescribed in a reference table (e.g., 15 days, 1 month, 2 months/4 months, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies short-form timeline commitments and refers to instruction/enforcement rule articles for exact references; unavoidable exceptions must be reported up the chain.

rubrics_metrics.name: General principles for law application (transitional measures)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the revision of the Patent Act is made while the application is pending, transitional measures are introduced to prevent disadvantages; provisions of law shall be applied as of the filing date. Divisional/converted applications and applications filed by lawful right holders are deemed filed on the parent filing date, so laws are applied as of the parent filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures applicants are not disadvantaged by law changes during pendency; gives example regarding filing dates around statutory amendment cutoff.
